findings.title: InteLogix opens new contact centre in New Cairo
findings.summary: BPO operator InteLogix inaugurated a new contact-centre facility in New Cairo, with a ribbon-cutting ceremony attended by InteLogix President & CEO Mario Baddour, ITIDA CEO Ahmed Elzaher, and industry analyst Peter Ryan. The company said the New Cairo centre "combines advanced infrastructure with multilingual talent and a competitive delivery model," building on InteLogix's existing Egyptian operations to serve client contact-centre and outsourcing needs across the broader region. This lands the same cycle as Concentrix's previously-logged $1bn commitment to grow its Egypt CX/BPO workforce from 24,500 to 35,000 by 2028 (4 Sep dossier), a second independent data point that Egypt's multilingual talent pool and government-backed tech ecosystem (via ITIDA) are actively attracting fresh contact-centre investment, not just retaining existing capacity.

findings.title: QIIB wins two International Business Magazine 2026 awards
findings.summary: Qatar International Islamic Bank (QIIB) received two 2026 awards from International Business Magazine: Best Islamic Retail Service – Qatar, and Best Islamic Digital Banking Solution – Qatar. The judging panel credited QIIB's "leadership and ability to reshape the retail banking experience through advanced digital channels," alongside its operational efficiency in adopting new financial technology. QIIB frames its strategy around a "smart, personalised banking ecosystem" letting customers open accounts, access financing and manage payments digitally, with its mobile app as the centrepiece. This extends a pattern MECSC has tracked through 2026 of Qatari banks sweeping digital-CX award categories, QNB (Best Retail Bank for Digital Customer Experience) and Commercial Bank (Best Use of AI in Financial Services) both won comparable 2026 recognitions earlier in the year. Three different Qatari banks now hold three different digital-CX accolades in the same calendar year, worth flagging as a national pattern rather than an isolated result.

findings.title: stc Bahrain appoints Khalid Alia as Chief Digital and Customer Experience Officer
findings.summary: stc Bahrain named Khalid Alia as its new Chief Digital and Customer Experience Officer. Alia was previously Senior Director of Consumer Marketing and Customer Experience at stc Bahrain, where he "drove the company's consumer strategy, enhancing the customer journey" across multiple product launches. The company said he will now lead digital innovation and adoption initiatives, developing solutions aligned with evolving customer requirements. The appointment lands amid stc Bahrain's broader CX build-out, including its OneCX training partnership with the CX Clinic and the phased rollout of its dialect-native AI assistant Bayan (both previously logged), suggesting a leadership structure being put in place specifically to own that programme going forward.

findings.title: MEBIS 2026 banking-innovation summit convenes in Dubai
findings.summary: The Middle East Banking Innovation Summit (MEBIS) 2026 ran 16–17 September at Jumeirah Emirates Towers, Dubai, with more than 500 pre-registrations and banking leaders from the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Egypt and Jordan expected to attend. The summit's central theme was the shift from generative AI assistants to agentic AI systems capable of executing tasks independently across platforms, a shift organisers framed as raising new governance and accountability questions rather than being purely a capability upgrade. Sessions also covered infrastructure modernisation, real-time/cross-border payments, data-governance strategy, and, directly relevant to members, balancing automation with personalisation, security and trust in digital banking customer experience. The accountability framing here is worth reading alongside this run's Global Trends Note: global contact-centre-AI commentary from the same week is making an almost identical argument (deployment volume no longer proves value; resolution quality and governance do), a sign the regional banking-AI conversation and the global CX-AI conversation are converging on the same maturity-stage concern at the same time.

findings.title: DOO's Arabic-dialect-native AI customer experience platform gains GCC traction
findings.summary: Bahrain-based AI platform DOO continues to scale its Arabic-first approach to enterprise customer experience, built around its proprietary OMLAQ engine, which is designed to understand and respond in regional dialects, Bahraini, Saudi, Kuwaiti, Emirati and others, rather than delivering mechanically translated responses. Beyond conversation, the platform offers multi-channel integration (WhatsApp, Instagram, websites), sentiment analysis via its Pulse engine, and workflow automation including customer categorisation and ticket routing. Since founding in 2024, DOO reports serving over 60 enterprise customers across telecommunications, airlines, banking and e-commerce in four GCC countries, growing ARR by 1,200%, securing $1.7M in seed funding, and signing a $2M+ partnership with Total CX. This is a third independent data point, after stc Bahrain's Bayan and Kuwait's Warba Bank "Bdr AI" (both previously logged), that dialect-native fluency specifically, not generic Arabic-language support, is becoming an explicit vendor-selection criterion for GCC enterprises deploying conversational AI.

findings.title: Dubai Duty Free and Emirates strike exclusive passenger-benefits agreement
findings.summary: Dubai Duty Free (DDF) and Emirates formalised an exclusive partnership offering special discounts to Emirates passengers travelling through or to Dubai, focused on enhancing the airport shopping experience at DDF's Terminal 3 retail locations at Dubai International Airport. Senior executives from both organisations signed the agreement, which both parties described as "a shared commitment... to enhance the passenger experience on the ground, support Dubai's tourism and aviation sector, and grow traffic to and through Dubai across the Emirates network." Framed as a commercial loyalty-style tie-up rather than a new store format or renovation, but it's a clean, dated passenger-CX case study for members tracking how Gulf airports and their travel-retail partners are packaging experience benefits directly into the airline relationship rather than relying on walk-in footfall alone.

findings.title: Doha Festival City wins "Best Mall" at Visit Qatar's Hala Summer Shopping Festival Awards
findings.summary: Doha Festival City was named "Best Mall" at Visit Qatar's Hala Summer Shopping Festival Awards, recognising what the organiser called "exceptional contribution to the national initiative, driven by its outstanding visitor engagement, guest turnout, and innovative marketing." The mall's summer campaign included an exclusive Disney's Moana activation, street parades, a Shop & Win promotional campaign and daily family-oriented performances, which the mall credits with strong footfall through the Hala Summer 2026 season.

findings.title: Knowledge Economic City accelerates five-district Madinah masterplan into delivery
findings.summary: Knowledge Economic City (member) is advancing its 6.8 million sqm Madinah masterplan, designed for 200,000 residents and 42,000 hotel rooms, across five complementary districts. CEO Dr Moath Al-Yahya described the company as "a destination developer building a city within a city." Al Alyaa, the residential community, has reached 100% structural completion on select buildings with 1,490 premium units on sale; Madinah Gate, the transit-oriented district linked to the Haramain High-Speed Railway, now has its DoubleTree by Hilton hotel open; the 980,000 sqm Islamic World District (targeting 20,000 hotel rooms) has Clusters 1 and 2 under construction; and Multaqa AlMadinah, a leisure-destination partnership with Alrashid Properties, is advancing with multiple hotel brands. KEC's pipeline now exceeds 11,000 hotel rooms with Hilton, Marriott, Hyatt and Radisson.

findings.title: Cenomi Centers CEO: 2026 is the peak investment year; 2028 targets reaffirmed
findings.summary: In an interview with Argaam, Cenomi Centers (member) CEO Alison Rehill-Erguven said "2026 marks the peak of the company's investment phase," after which financing expenses and operating margins are expected to improve as major projects, chiefly Westfield Jeddah (opened July 2026) and Westfield Riyadh, transition from construction into revenue-generating operation. The CEO reaffirmed the company's 2028 targets of SAR 3.4–3.6 billion revenue and SAR 2.5–2.6 billion EBITDA, representing roughly 60% growth versus 2025, and described the company as "well positioned to meet its targets through disciplined execution."
